title: Preserving irregular pulse timing with classic Lomb–Scargle does not improve pooled PPG respiratory estimates in two cohorts
abstract: Classic Lomb–Scargle pooling of three irregularly timed PPG respiratory modulations did not improve respiratory-rate estimation over interpolated rectangular Fourier pooling in two independent cohorts. Equal-record MAE was 4.381 versus 3.948 breaths/min in BIDMC and 3.599 versus 2.800 in CapnoBase. Comparator-minus-Lomb gains were -0.432 (95% record-bootstrap CI -0.863 to -0.003) and -0.799 (-1.845 to 0.214), respectively. These previously exposed datasets support an exploratory negative implementation result, not rejection of all uneven-sampling methods.
